name: Sidetic
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Merlin, Stella & Valerio Pisaniello. 2025. "Late Languages of Marginal Attestation: Pamphylian, Sidetic, and Pisidian." In Contacts of Languages and Peoples in the Hittite and Post-Hittite World, 360-380. Leiden: Brill.
sources.note: Most recent synthesis of Sidetic grammar/phonology; open-access license (CC BY-NC-ND) per Crossref, so a browser download should work even though brill.com blocks our network; the one place a modern statement on (un)knowability of Sidetic accent would appear.

sources.citation: Kassian, A. S. 2013. "Sidetskij jazyk." In Jazyki mira: Reliktovye indoevropejskie jazyki Perednej i Central'noj Azii, 175-177. Moskva: Academia.
sources.note: The Glottolog-listed sketch in the Languages of the World series, whose template normally carries an explicit line on udarenie (stress) even when unknown.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Sidetic language" (accessed 2026-09-17), used only for its bibliography
sources.note: No phonology beyond 'aphaeresis is frequent in names in Sidetic.. as is syncope'; no stress statement. Supplied the bibliography (Pérez Orozco, Zinko & Zinko 2019, Merlin & Pisaniello 2025, Kassian 2013, Nollé, Neumann, Rizza 2005, Kadmos 2025 papers).

sources.citation: Kloekhorst, Alwin. 2022. "Anatolian." In Thomas Olander (ed.), The Indo-European Language Family: A Phylogenetic Perspective, 63-82. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (Open Access). doi:10.1017/9781108758666.005
sources.note: Nothing on Sidetic stress. Sidetic is described on p. 65 ('attested in some ten inscriptions on coins and stone.. The number of textual remains is very low, so we only know a few facts about Sidetic grammar and lexicon') and its subgrouping is discussed pp. 70-71; the only accent mention is a Proto-Anatolian sound law (PIE accented *ó lengthened, p. 67).

sources.citation: Woudhuizen, Fred C. 2020. "On the Reading and Interpretation of the Two Longer Sidetic Inscriptions S I.2.1 and S I.2.5." Živa Antika 70(1-2): 17-34. doi:10.47054/ZIVA20701-2017w
sources.note: Silent: discusses sign values (vowel /a/, sibilants, punctuation strokes) and readings of two inscriptions; a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/prosody gives zero hits in the 18-page text.

sources.citation: Pandey, Anshuman. 2019. "Introducing the Sidetic Script." Unicode document L2/19-106, 2 pp.
sources.note: Script-encoding note only; nothing on the language's phonology or stress.

sources.citation: eDiAna (Digital Philological-Etymological Dictionary of the Minor Ancient Anatolian Corpus Languages), LMU Munich, corpus page
sources.note: Corpus page confirms a Sidetic corpus (2021) numbered after Nollé 2001: 625-646 and cites Zinko & Zinko 2019; no language description or stress statement visible.

sources.citation: Zinko, Christian & Michaela Zinko. 2019. "Sidetisch – Ein Update zu Schrift und Sprache." In R. I. Kim, J. Mynářová & P. Pavúk (eds.), Hrozný and Hittite: The First Hundred Years, 416-432. Leiden: Brill.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Current standard update on script and language, the sign list Woudhuizen 2020 and eDiAna rely on.

sources.citation: Pérez Orozco, Santiago. 2007. "Propuesta de nueva valoración fonética de los signos sidéticos." Kadmos 46: 125-142.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The main phonetic re-evaluation of the Sidetic signary; any remark on vowel quantity/accent would be here.

sources.citation: Nollé, Johannes. 2001. Side im Altertum: Geschichte und Zeugnisse, Band II (Inschriften griechischer Städte aus Kleinasien 44), corpus of Sidetic inscriptions pp. 625-646. Bonn: Habelt.

sources.note: The corpus edition of record (eDiAna numbering follows it); contains the fullest linguistic commentary on the inscriptions.

sources.citation: Neumann, Günter. 1978. "Die sidetische Schrift." Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, Classe di Lettere e Filosofia III.8(3): 869-886.

sources.note: 'Este artículo representa un reexamen del corpus sidético y su interpretación basada en la propuesta de nuevos valores para algunos signos.' A 27-page synthesis update of the whole language; its phonology will be graphemic/segmental (sign values, vowel and consonant inventory, aphaeresis/syncope in adapted Greek names). No tone statement expected: Sidetic is known from about a dozen short alphabetic inscriptions and coin legends with no prosodic notation, so lexical tone or accent placement is unrecoverable; at most the paper may say so or comment on syncope/aphaeresis as indirect accent evid…
